title: What Subfloor Prep Is Needed Before Installing Hardwood Floors?
meta: Hardwood subfloor prep in Everett: flat to 3/16 in over 10 ft, dry, clean and screwed tight. What each subfloor type needs and how Wills Flooring checks it.
keywords: subfloor prep for hardwood floors, subfloor requirements hardwood installation, how flat does subfloor need to be for hardwood, plywood subfloor moisture hardwood, hardwood installation Everett WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Before hardwood goes down, the subfloor has to be flat to within 3/16 in over 10 ft, dry (plywood under 12% moisture, concrete tested), clean, structurally sound and screwed tight to the joists.
blocks.detail: Those are the industry standards every hardwood manufacturer writes into its warranty. Wills Flooring checks all five at the free estimate, so the $3.25 per sq ft installation labor comes with a written list of any prep your Everett floor actually needs.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks why an installer wants to "fix the subfloor" when the old carpet came up and the plywood looks fine. The honest answer is that a subfloor problem never shows up on day one. It shows up in six months as a squeak, a gap that opens every winter, or a hollow-sounding spot in the hallway. In Everett we see two very different subfloors: 1900s to 1920s diagonal plank in Riverside and Bayside, and 1990s to 2000s OSB or plywood in Silver Lake and Eastmont. Both can take hardwood beautifully, but they need different prep, and this post explains exactly what we look for.

blocks.text: The five checks we make on every Everett subfloor

items.title: 1. Flat, not level
items.text: Flat means no humps or dips beyond 3/16 in across a 10 ft straightedge (or 1/8 in across 6 ft). Level means parallel to the ground, and nobody cares about that. Old Everett houses have settled; we flatten the surface, not the house.

items.title: 2. Dry
items.text: Plywood or OSB should read 12% moisture or less, and within 4% of the hardwood we are installing (2% for planks wider than 3 in). Concrete gets a calcium chloride or in-slab relative humidity test. Port Gardner air keeps Everett crawlspaces damp, so this test fails more often than people expect.

items.title: 3. Structurally sound
items.text: No soft spots, delamination, rot or water staining. We probe around exterior doors, under old radiators and next to bathrooms. A soft 2 by 2 ft patch gets cut out and replaced, not covered.

items.title: 4. Fastened tight
items.text: Loose subfloor is the number one cause of squeaks. We screw the existing sheets down every 6 in along edges and 12 in in the field before a single hardwood board is nailed, which also quiets floors that already squeak.

items.title: 5. Clean and free of old adhesive
items.text: Carpet tack strip, staples, drywall mud, paint overspray and old vinyl adhesive all get scraped. A single staple under a solid board telegraphs as a bump you will feel in socks.

items.title: Thickness and joist spacing
items.text: Nail-down hardwood needs at least 3/4 in (23/32 in) plywood over joists 16 in on center, or 7/8 in over 19.2 in. Thinner 5/8 in sheets found in some 1970s Everett split-levels get a second layer of 3/8 in plywood.

a.title: Pay for this prep

Replacing any soft or delaminated sheet

Ripping out sound 3/4 in plywood to install new plywood
Leveling a floor to a bubble instead of flattening it
Sealing plywood with paint or primer, which does nothing for hardwood
Thick foam underlayment under nail-down hardwood

blocks.title: Everett crawlspaces:
blocks.text: Half the moisture failures we see on the north end come from the crawlspace, not the subfloor. If there is no 6 mil vapor barrier on the dirt, or the vents are blocked, the plywood will read 14% to 16% all winter and the new hardwood will cup. Fix the crawlspace first; it costs less than the floor.
Questions to ask before anyone nails a board

items.html: Did you measure moisture, and what did it read? The number should be on the estimate. If nobody pulled out a meter, the warranty language about "proper site conditions" is working against you.
Where is the floor out of flat, and by how much? A straightedge takes five minutes. A vague "we will level it" line without a location is a guess, and guesses get billed twice.
Will you screw the subfloor before installing? This is the cheapest squeak insurance there is, and it is standard on every Wills Flooring hardwood installation.
What is under the carpet? If the answer is particleboard, the price has to include removal. If it is diagonal plank, ask about direction or an overlay.

Is prep a separate line on the quote? We list every prep item with a price so the $3.25 per sq ft labor stays clean and you can compare quotes fairly. See how long an Everett install takes once prep is done.

faq.q: How flat does a subfloor need to be for hardwood flooring?
faq.a: The industry standard is 3/16 in over a 10 ft span, or 1/8 in over 6 ft. Anything more than that gets sanded down if it is a hump, or filled with cement patch or self-leveler if it is a dip. Flat is not the same as level; old Everett houses that slope can still take hardwood as long as the surface is smooth.

faq.q: Can hardwood be installed over an old plank subfloor?
faq.a: Yes. The 1 by 6 diagonal planks in 1900s to 1940s Everett homes are a good base once loose boards are re-nailed and split ones replaced. Narrow solid strip can run perpendicular to the planks. Wider planks and engineered floors usually get a 3/8 in plywood overlay so the boards have continuous support.

faq.q: Do I have to remove particleboard before installing hardwood?
faq.a: Yes, always. Particleboard does not hold nails, glue bonds fail on it, and it swells if it ever gets damp. It has to come out and be replaced with 3/4 in plywood. This is common under 1970s and 1980s carpet in Everett and is priced as a prep item at the estimate.

faq.q: What moisture level should a subfloor be before hardwood?
faq.a: Plywood and OSB should read 12% or less, and be within 4% of the hardwood being installed (2% for planks wider than 3 in). Concrete needs a calcium chloride test under 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft in 24 hours or an in-slab relative humidity reading the adhesive maker accepts, often 75% to 80%.

faq.q: Does Wills Flooring charge extra for subfloor prep?
faq.a: Installation labor is $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid and $2.75 for unfinished. Prep such as tear-out, replacing sheets, self-leveler and overlays is listed separately on the written quote from the free estimate, so you know the full number before we start.

faq.q: Can I skip prep if the floor is going to be floated or glued instead of nailed?
faq.a: No. Floating and glue-down floors are even less forgiving of an uneven surface because there is no nail pulling the board down. Flatness, moisture and cleanliness rules are the same. Glue-down also needs old adhesive and paint scraped off so the new adhesive bonds to bare plywood or concrete.
